title: The Gettysburg Address
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Abraham Lincoln gave this short speech on November 19, 1863, at the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, four and a half months after the battle there. It takes about two minutes to say and is one of the most famous speeches in American history, which makes it a classic piece of memory work.

How to hold it: Narrate it first: read it aloud and say what each paragraph does. The first looks back to 1776, the second looks at the battlefield, and the third looks ahead. Those three are your big chunks. Inside each, learn three or four phrases at a time and recite with the page covered. Lincoln built the speech on patterns that help memory: three in a row (dedicate, consecrate, hallow; of the people, by the people, for the people) and pairs (living and dead; say here, did here). Picture each phrase on a walk across the field, and come back on day 1, 3, 7 and 21.
